lines: Ladder Master Sabine: Welcome to the Glasswind Ladder. Eight Wayfarers, one rung each, no skipping, no crying on the rungs.
Ladder Master Sabine: Six rungs stand out on the flats. Seven and eight wait in here. Climb all eight and the purse is yours.
Ladder Master Sabine: Three thousand coins. Nobody has ever collected. That's not a warning, that's a statistic.
Ladder Master Sabine: Still climbing? Good. Falling is free, climbing is the part with dignity.
Ladder Master Sabine: You beat Dario. My own son. I'm so proud I could cry. On the purse, mostly.
Ladder Master Sabine: Here it is. Do read rule nine on the back, dear. Everybody skips rule nine.

sabine_after: Ladder Master Sabine: The ladder's open again. Same rules. Fewer, after you.
purse_caught: You hold up the promise Old Pell made her write on the ladder board. In chalk, signed, witnessed by a goat.
Sabine: Rule nine says the purse goes to the house. Rule ten, apparently, says the goat outranks me. Fine. Take it.
purse_struck: Rule nine, in very small letters: 'The purse remains property of the house. The winner may keep the feeling.'
Sabine: And the bouncers would like a word about your attitude. Several words. With Spirlings.
bouncers_defeat: Bouncer: We'll put you down as 'left voluntarily'. Here's the consolation purse. It's mostly buttons.
bouncers_lose: The bouncers walk you to the door, then a bit further. The desert is very big when you're carried.
ledger_purse: Sabine promised three thousand coins to whoever climbed her ladder, then pointed at rule nine on the back of the purse.

lines: THE GLASSWIND LADDER - eight rungs, one purse. Rule one: no biting. Rules two to eight: see rule one.
THE GLASSWIND LADDER. Under it, in fresh chalk: 'The purse goes to the winner. S.' And a hoof print.
Bell-Mender Hesper: Caravans used to follow the Bell Line across the flats. One bell per post, one post per mile, nobody lost.
Bell-Mender Hesper: Then the bells went missing. Nine of them. Bring them back and I'll hang them again. Safe roads for everyone.
Bell-Mender Hesper: Any bells? Five lie out on the flats. The rest, they say, went into the Mirage Kiln. Bells don't walk, so somebody carried them.
Bell-Mender Hesper: All nine! Listen to them. Like nine little liars clearing their throats. I mean choirboys. Choirboys.
Bell-Mender Hesper: I'll hang them on the posts tonight. Take this for your trouble.
Bell-Mender Hesper: Hear that? The Bell Line rings again. Driver Ott will tell you how much the caravans love it.
Bell-Mender Hesper: You read my ledger. Rude. I only moved the posts a little. A mile here, a mile there, into the kiln.
Bell-Mender Hesper: Venn pays per caravan. Safe roads were never the business. Lost ones are.

hesper_defeat: Bell-Mender Hesper: Fine. I'll move the posts back. Do you know how heavy a post is? Neither do I, I always had the crew carry them.
hesper_lose: Bell-Mender Hesper: Ring, ring. That's the sound of you going the wrong way.

lines: Bell-Mender Hesper: The bells ring true now. Terrible for business. Mine, I mean.
Driver Ott: Twenty years on the flats. Lost four camels, two wives and one very good hat.
Driver Ott: The new bells? They ring at the wrong posts. Follow them and you end up at the Mirage Kiln, every time.
Driver Ott: Nobody follows a bell into a kiln by accident twice. Go see what's in there.
Driver Ott: That little girl with the twin? Funny. No child crosses the flats alone. Not with a clean dress and all her teeth.

ott_plain: Driver Ott: Water, shade, and never trust a shortcut. That's the whole desert, kid.

lines: Tamsin: My twin brother Tavi walked into the Mirage Kiln to look at the shiny glass. He didn't come out.
Tamsin: Could you find him? He's easy to spot. He looks exactly like me, but worse.
Tamsin: His scarf! So he's alive. Probably. Mostly. Let me take you to him myself, I know the way.
Tamsin: Meet me at the kiln door. Come alone. Tavi's shy.

tamsin_wait: Tamsin: Tavi's somewhere in the kiln. Look for something with a bad knot in it. He never learned knots.

lines: Tamsin: You came! And alone. That's the important part. Tavi's just round the back. Close your eyes, it's a surprise.

tamsin_after: Tamsin: Dad says lookouts get a tenth. I get a tenth of nothing now. Thanks a lot.
twin_caught: You keep your eyes open. Round the back: three Sandglass Crew with a net and no twin.
Tamsin: ...Ott told you, didn't he. Fine. There's no Tavi. The scarf's from the crew's lost and found. Here, have my cut. It's small.
twin_struck: You close your eyes. A net drops. Tamsin's voice: 'Sorry! There's no Tavi. There's a finder's fee.'
crew_defeat: Crew Uncle Brask: Out-fought by the mark. Venn will dock us. Tamsin, you're grounded.
crew_lose: The crew empties your pockets and leaves you a receipt shaped like a glass bead.
ledger_twin: Little Tamsin sent you into the kiln for a twin brother, then led you round the back to the Sandglass Crew's net.

lines: Naturalist Ilse: I'm writing the first honest field guide of the Glasswind. Where every kind lives, to the rock.
Naturalist Ilse: Bring me eight kinds in your team so I can sketch them. They don't have to smile. Most don't.
Naturalist Ilse: The guide sold out before it was printed. One buyer. Paid in advance. Very keen on the maps.
Naturalist Ilse: You took my notes off a poacher? I sold them to a 'collector'. Same thing, it turns out, with fewer cages.
Naturalist Ilse: I'll write a second edition. With the wrong rocks in it.
Naturalist Ilse: A Rollibex! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Sirocat! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Noonwhist! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Velvessa! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Caravant! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Obelith! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Fulgorin! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: A Wadishell! Hold still. No, the other still.
Naturalist Ilse: Eight! The guide is done. Every kind, every den, every rock. Here, a lens for your trouble.

ilse_more: Naturalist Ilse: Still missing some. Four live out on the flats, four in the kiln. The kiln ones bite more.

lines: Innkeeper Zohra: Beds, water, shade. The shade is free. The rest is also free, if you don't look at the bill.
Innkeeper Zohra: Your Spirlings look baked. Let them rest.
Supplier Kasim: Tonics, brews, sand out of your boots for free. Everything else, list price.
trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew power_brew focus_brew

lines: Guide Varro: Varro. Best guide on the Glasswind. Ask anyone. Well, ask anyone who came back.
Guide Varro: I know a shortcut through the mirage, straight to the kiln. Half the walk. Trust me?

varro_after: Guide Varro: No hard feelings. The desert does what it wants. I just help it along.
varro_betray: Varro's shortcut ends in a dune bowl. Three Sand Bandits wait at the bottom with a picnic and a price list.
Guide Varro: Half the walk, I said. I never said which half.
varro_reward: The shortcut is real. Halfway down it Varro digs up a crate of old crew loot and splits it with you. Mostly fairly.
varro_kept: The shortcut is a long cut. Varro swears the dunes moved. They may have.
bandits_defeat: Sand Bandit: We'll tell Varro you were a bad investment. He'll understand. He's one too.
bandits_lose: The bandits take your snacks and leave you the map. The map is of somewhere else.

lines: Signalman Oren: Three heliographs warn the caravans of sandstorms. Flash, flash, run. Simple.
Signalman Oren: But they've drifted. Turn each one to face the sun again, would you? My knees don't do posts anymore.
Signalman Oren: All three! Flash, flash, flash. That's not 'storm', by the way. That's 'fat caravan, two guards, come now'.
Signalman Oren: Venn thanks you. I'd thank you too, but you'd only try to stop me. So let's skip to that.
Signalman Oren: Two more posts to go. Mind the sun, it's out to get you. Like everyone.

oren_defeat: Signalman Oren: Fine. I'll flash 'storm' for real. Caravans will hide, the crew will starve. Everyone's unhappy. Balance.
oren_lose: Signalman Oren: Flash, flash. That one means 'idiot'.
oren_after: Signalman Oren: Storm warnings only now. I even mean some of them.

lines: A man in glass-dust chains: 'Thank the sun. I'm Venn, the glassmaster. The crew keeps me here to make their fakes.'
Glassmaster Venn: The key hangs by the door. Unlock me, quick, before they come back.
Glassmaster Venn: Well. The chains were glass too. Everything in here is. Shall we see what you're made of?

venn_defeat: Glassmaster Venn: Cracked. All of it. The bells, the mirrors, the girl, the guide. Do you know how long it takes to build a good lie in this heat?
Glassmaster Venn: Take the gallery key. Sell the glass. Everyone else did.
venn_lose: Glassmaster Venn: Shattered. Sweep yourself up on the way out.
venn_after: Glassmaster Venn: I'm going into honest glass. Windows. Nobody ever lied through a window. Well. Rarely.
chains_caught: You remember Hesper's ledger: 'V. takes half.' You leave the key where it is.
Glassmaster Venn shrugs out of the chains himself. 'Worth a try. Most people are kinder than you.'
chains_struck: The key turns. The chains fall away, and so does the gallery door behind you, locked from outside.
Glassmaster Venn: Thank you! Crew, the kind one's in. Bill them for the rescue.
trap_defeat: Crew Muscle: That's three of us down for one rescuer. Venn's maths never adds up.
trap_lose: The crew carries you out and leaves you by the bell posts. Ring if you need anything.
ledger_chains: Venn played the crew's prisoner in his own gallery and asked you to unlock chains he could slip any time.
